name: Charcoal Typhoon
affiliation_detail:
Trend Micro (2022) described Charcoal Typhoon/Earth Lusca as a "threat actor originating from China," with IP source region "near Sichuan, Chengdu, China." 
ESET (2025) identified the group as "FishMonger" and linked it to i-Soon, the Chinese contractor whose employees were charged by the DOJ in March 2025 for espionage campaigns from 2016 to 2023. The i-Soon leak (February 2024) revealed the contractor's role managing offensive teams aligned with this group's operations. 
FBI's wanted list directly associates eight i-Soon employees and two MPS officers to Aquatic Panda. However, the DOJ indictment does not specifically list any aliases.
entity_name: i-Soon (Anxun Information Technology, 安洵信息)
description:
Charcoal Typhoon is a Chinese state-linked espionage group active since at least 2019 with a "dual mission of intelligence gathering and economic espionage" with "persistence, operational intensity, and global reach." (Recorded Future, 2023)
The group targets government institutions, telecommunications, academia, media, religious organizations, COVID-19 research, gambling companies, and cryptocurrency platforms across 17+ countries. It operates under the broader Winnti ecosystem but maintains separate infrastructure, (Trend Micro, 2022) and has been directly linked to the Chinese contractor i-Soon. (ESET, 2025)
The group uses a multi-tiered infrastructure separating reconnaissance from long-term C2, and employs both shared Winnti tools and bespoke malware.  Recorded Future noted the group's "persistence, operational intensity, and global reach" across campaigns spanning 17 countries in three years. Some operations appear financially motivated, targeting cryptocurrency exchanges and gambling platforms.

campaigns.name: RedHotel Global Campaign (17 Countries)
campaigns.description: Recorded Future documented sustained campaigns across 17 countries targeting government, academia, telecommunications, media, and research.  Used stolen code-signing certificates, compromised government infrastructure for C2, and a mix of ShadowPad, FunnySwitch, Spyder, Winnti, Cobalt Strike, and Brute Ratel C4.

campaigns.name: Operation FishMedley (2022)
campaigns.description: ESET documented a 10-month campaign against seven targets across government, NGOs, and think tanks in Taiwan, Thailand, Hungary, France, Turkey, and other countries. ESET linked the campaign to i-Soon oversight. SodaMaster (previously associated with APT10) was shared across groups.
